findings: B9-PARALLEL-CONTACT: Rust uses event_y_positions (message stroke/callback ordinate) as the common parallel contact for all message kinds. Java aligns component getYPoint, which for a self component is text height plus half of the 13-unit loop plus paddingX, whereas ordinary arrows use text height plus paddingY. These are separate from the self callback's activation-dependent p1/p2. The fresh chain and multiline controls leave ordinary messages and their activation starts 2.5 units too high while the self component matches. This is not a label-metric discrepancy. Next repair: Represent tile contact, drawing origin, callback ordinates and extent below contact separately, and compose their maxima exactly as TileParallel; do not add a case-specific 2.5 offset.

B9-PARALLEL-PREDECESSOR: Java's first parallel tile captures the preceding graphical tile plus trailing life tiles, even when that predecessor is a standalone note. Rust clears parallel_members on the note and therefore serializes the following & message. The fresh case is 225px high versus Java 199px, with deactivation delayed along with the message. Command parallel ancestry is retained but graphical parallel composition is not. Next repair: Compose the immediate prior tile (including NoteTile) and suffix LifeEventTiles, without treating a standalone note as a barrier to parallel layout. Preserve the distinct rule that notes can reset stairs paint state.

B9-DESTROY-ORDER: The created participant's nested return/destroy case has matching coordinates and colors but wrong primitive order. Java draws a level's closing destroy immediately after that level's bar before traversing the next level. Rust stores segments and destroys in separate vectors and emits all bars before any cross. Expected outer bar, two destroy strokes, inner bar becomes outer bar, inner bar, two destroy strokes. The strict comparator correctly rejects order, which can affect overlap in other inputs. Next repair: Return an ordered draw stream or preserve per-level close-decoration attachment through materialization; do not post-sort the generated SVG.
